title: Heavy flooding
description: A 1-in-100-year storm tide today (1.60 m AHD, also the major flood level at the Southbank gauge) with heavy rain. Typical water on flooded footpaths reaches the thigh. A static estimate, not a hydraulic model: no flow or velocity. River flows can raise Southbank levels above the bay tide level.
sources: Level: typical (median) depth on flooded footpaths over the thigh, up to the hip; body landmarks after Drillis & Contini (1966), as used to grade flood depth by Feng, Brenner & Sester (2020).

Mechanisms: Melbourne Water, Southbank Precinct Local Floodplain Development Plan (2026): river flooding from storm tide and river flows; local stormwater flooding, shallow but widespread, made worse when high tailwater stops the drains discharging.

Storm tide levels for Port Phillip Bay: GHD for Melbourne Water (2017), Fishermans Bend: Baseline drainage plan options, Table 1: 5-year 1.10, 20-year 1.25, 100-year 1.60 m AHD; 100-year in 2100 2.40 m AHD.

Drain backflow: City of Melbourne Municipal Emergency Management Plan, Flood and Storm Sub-plan (2025): a high tide reduces the drains' capacity to discharge and backflow surcharges around the drainage pits; rain over 20 mm/h for an hour or more is likely to cause flash flooding.
Stormwater ponding: closed depressions of the ground model, anywhere in the area.
Drain inlets: City of Melbourne open data, Stormwater Pits (CC BY 4.0), surface inlets only.
Ground: Geoscience Australia 5 m LiDAR digital elevation model (CC BY 4.0).
